metadata.title: Navigating the impact of the pandemic on teacher competencies: A comparative analysis across economic contexts using pre- and post-COVID-19 PISA data

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA teacher background instruments from two teacher databases (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ and CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) merged on common variables, covering 2019 (pre-COVID) and 2023 (post-COVID) teacher responses across 24 countries. The manuscript does not report the use of PISA sampling/survey weights or any replicate-weight procedure, and it does not name any weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate design (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the analysis relies on mean comparisons and structural equation modeling rather than ML algorithms that natively support complex-survey weighting, the weighting approach is unclear; readers should verify in the original PISA documentation or supplementary materials whether weights were applied. For replication, analysts should use the appropriate PISA teacher sampling weights and, if available, replicate weights for variance estimation when producing cross-country and pre/post comparisons.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables are teacher competency and professional development need constructs derived from 28 PISA items rated on Likert-type scales, validated via CFA and analyzed via mean comparisons and SEM. These constructs are not reported as PV-based cognitive achievement scores, so plausible values are not applicable to the modeled outcomes. The manuscript also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure (e.g., complete-case selection or imputation), which is a reporting gap because PISA teacher questionnaires typically contain item nonresponse.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study analyzes PISA teacher data for 2019 (pre-COVID; dataset CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ) and 2023 (post-COVID) and merges two teacher databases (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ and CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) based on common variables. Beyond this merge, the manuscript does not report additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., grade restrictions, item-completion thresholds, or explicit complete-case criteria). It therefore uses the full available teacher sample for the specified 24 countries and the specified pre/post periods.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — teacher empowerment construct
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=3.23 (SD=0.59) vs 2023 Mean=3.36 (SD=0.58), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=3.61 (SD=0.46), UMICs Mean=3.48 (SD=0.52), HICs Mean=3.17 (SD=0.60), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): empowerment total effect TE=0.22 (DE=0.00, IE=0.23) for PDN; collaboration total effect TE=0.27 (DE=0.27, IE=0.00).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period, country economic level, professional development needs, and teacher collaboration to analyze empowerment-related competencies, finding that empowerment increased post-COVID (Mean 3.23→3.36, p=0.00) and varied by economic level (LMICs highest, p=0.00). This indicates that pandemic-era shifts in teacher professional learning and collaborative practices may strengthen empowerment competencies, though the study’s cross-sectional design limits causal claims about the pandemic’s direct effect.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — teacher management construct
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=3.30 (SD=0.59) vs 2023 Mean=3.40 (SD=0.57), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=3.52 (SD=0.50), UMICs Mean=3.46 (SD=0.55), HICs Mean=3.27 (SD=0.59), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): PDN total effect TE=0.21 (DE=0.00, IE=0.21); collaboration total effect TE=0.27 (DE=0.14, IE=0.00).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period, country economic level, professional development needs, and teacher collaboration to analyze management-related competencies, finding that management improved post-COVID (Mean 3.30→3.40, p=0.00) and was highest in LMICs (p=0.00). This indicates that targeted professional development and collaboration may help teachers strengthen classroom management practices after disruptions, while the absence of explicit causal identification means the pandemic effect cannot be confirmed.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — teacher adaptability construct
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=3.33 (SD=0.59) vs 2023 Mean=3.39 (SD=0.59), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=3.45 (SD=0.56), UMICs Mean=3.47 (SD=0.56), HICs Mean=3.28 (SD=0.60), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): PDN total effect TE=0.21 (DE=0.00, IE=0.21); collaboration total effect TE=0.00 (DE=0.00, IE=0.21).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period, country economic level, professional development needs, and teacher collaboration to analyze adaptability-related competencies, finding that adaptability increased post-COVID (Mean 3.33→3.39, p=0.00) with economic-level differences (p=0.00). This indicates that professional development and collaborative learning may support teachers’ instructional flexibility after crises, though the study’s cross-sectional comparison limits inference about whether these changes were caused by COVID-19.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — professional development needs (professionalism)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=2.83 (SD=0.80) vs 2023 Mean=2.81 (SD=0.84), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=2.59 (SD=0.87), UMICs Mean=2.67 (SD=0.88), HICs Mean=2.92 (SD=0.77), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): PDN construct shows strong shaping of professionalism needs (reported as PDN→professionalism needs with Beta=1.17 in text; Table 7 indicates professionalism DE=2.66, IE=0.00, TE=2.66).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period and country economic level to analyze professionalism-related professional development needs, finding a slight decline post-COVID (Mean 2.83→2.81, p=0.00) while needs remained highest in HICs (p=0.00). This indicates that post-pandemic professional development priorities may shift away from professionalism content toward other needs (e.g., inclusion), but the study cannot establish causal drivers of these shifts.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — professional development needs (inclusion)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=2.55 (SD=0.79) vs 2023 Mean=2.62 (SD=0.83), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=2.41 (SD=0.91), UMICs Mean=2.37 (SD=0.85), HICs Mean=2.72 (SD=0.75), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): PDN total effect TE=1.00 (DE=1.00, IE=0.00) for inclusion needs; collaboration total effect TE=0.42 (DE=0.00, IE=0.42).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period and country economic level to analyze inclusion-related professional development needs, finding that inclusion needs increased post-COVID (Mean 2.55→2.62, p=0.00) and were highest in HICs (p=0.00). This indicates that professional development systems should prioritize inclusion-focused training after disruptions, while recognizing that the study’s design does not prove that COVID-19 directly caused the increase.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2019 & 2023 Teacher questionnaire (CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ; CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ) — teacher collaboration construct
main_findings.performance_metrics: Pre/post mean change: 2019 Mean=4.42 (SD=1.14) vs 2023 Mean=4.51 (SD=1.16), p=0.00. By economic level (Table 3): LMICs Mean=3.37 (SD=1.25), UMICs Mean=4.34 (SD=1.16), HICs Mean=4.61 (SD=1.09), p=0.00. SEM effects (Table 7): PDN total effect TE=0.27 (DE=0.27, IE=0.00) on collaboration; collaboration is also modeled as influencing competencies (e.g., Beta=0.31 in text).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2019 & 2023 teacher questionnaire the study leveraged pre vs post COVID period, country economic level, and professional development needs to analyze collaboration in school, finding that collaboration increased post-COVID (Mean 4.42→4.51, p=0.00) and was highest in HICs (p=0.00). This indicates that strengthening professional learning communities and collaboration mechanisms may be a key lever for sustaining post-pandemic improvements in teacher competencies, though causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional pre/post comparison.

data.outcome_summary: This open-access study uses PISA teacher questionnaire data from 2019 (pre-COVID; CY07_MSU_TCH_QQQ) and 2023 (post-COVID) merged with CY08MSP_TCH_QQQ, covering 128,866 teachers across 24 countries grouped into LMICs, UMICs, and HICs. The analysis compares pre/post means and economic-level differences for six constructs (empowerment, management, adaptability, professionalism needs, inclusion needs, and collaboration) and reports SEM model fit (RMSEA=0.02; NFI=0.91; CFI=0.91; TLI=0.90). Key results show empowerment (3.23→3.36, p=0.00), management (3.30→3.40, p=0.00), adaptability (3.33→3.39, p=0.00), and collaboration (4.42→4.51, p=0.00) increasing post-COVID, while professionalism needs slightly decline (2.83→2.81, p=0.00) and inclusion needs rise (2.55→2.62, p=0.00). Professional development needs and collaboration are modeled as positively associated with competencies (e.g., collaboration Beta=0.31 in text). Limitations include reliance on self-reported measures, unclear missing-data handling, and cross-sectional pre/post design that restricts causal claims about COVID-19.
